meetings.title: 6th Meeting 2026
meetings.summary: In this meeting the Committee reviewed matters submitted to the Committee by Members of the People's Majlis. The first on the agenda was the issue submitted by MP Mohamed Ibrahim of North Galolhu Constitunecy, regarding the current state of the traditional art of Feyli weaving in the Maldives and its preservation and promotion. As the committee had previously met with relevant authorities concerning this matter, it was decided to dispatch the necessary letters to the ministries and provide a formal response to the member who submitted the issue. Subsequently, the committee reviewed a matter submitted by the MP Ibrahim Hussain of South Fuvahmulah Constituency, alleging systemic harassment to a teacher at Fuvahmulah School by the school's principal. Upon seeking clarification from the Ministry of Education, Higher Education, and Skills Development, the Ministry informed the committee that the issue has now been resolved. Following deliberations, the committee decided to provide a response to the member stating that the matter has been resolved. The motion was passed unanimously by the members present at the time of voting. (Voting details are provided in the “Votes” section of this page.) The committee then discussed the matter referred by MP Mohamed Ibrahim of North Galolhu Constitunecy raising concerns on the renovation work of the old and former Thalassemia Centre building. Following discussions on this matter, MP Azim Abdul Azeez of Villingili Constituency proposed and MP Hamad Abdulla of North Fuvahmulah Constituency seconded to send letters to Male’ City Group of Hospitals to clarify about the renovvantion works. The motion was passed unanimously by the members present at the time of voting. (Voting details are provided in the “Votes” section of this page.) The meeting then proceeded to review the issue submitted by MP Mohamed Ibrahim of North Galolhu Constituency, seeking a solution to the problems arising from the high density of land transport vehicles in Male' City. Following discussions on this matter MP Saudulla Hilmy of North Thinadhoo Constituency proposed and MP Azim Abdul Azeez of Villingili Constituency seconded to send letters to the Male' City Council and the Ministry of Economic Development, Transport, and Trade to clarify regarding this issue. The motion was passed unanimously by the members present at the time of voting. (Voting details are provided in the “Votes” section of this page.)

meetings.title: 4th Meeting 2026
meetings.summary: In this meeting the Committee reviewed matters submitted to the Committee by Members of the People's Majlis. In this regard, the Committee discussed the issue submitted by MP Mohamed Ibrahim of North Galolhu Constituency, regarding the current status of the craft of Feyli weaving in Maldives, as well as its promotion and preservation. To clarify information regarding this matter, MP Hussain Sameer of of Thoddoo Constituency, proposed to meet with the Ministry of Economic Development, Transport and Trade, the Ministry of Arts, Culture and Heritage, the National Center for Cultural Heritage, and Mr. Ibrahim Aboobakurufulhu, an artisan in the field of Feyli weaving. This proposal was seconded by MP Ismail Shafeeu, Member for Isdhoo Constituency. The motion was passed unanimously by the members present at the time of voting. (Voting details are provided in the “Votes” section of this page.) Next the Committee discussed the matter submitted by MP Mohamed Ibrahim of North Galolhu Constituency, stating that the services provided by the Ministry of Transport and Civil Aviation have been consolidated into a single portal and outsourced to a company. In this regard, MP Hamad Abdulla of North Fuvahmulah Constituency, proposed, and MP Hussain Sameer of Thoddoo Constituency, seconded, to share the response provided by the Ministry of Transport and Civil Aviation regarding this matter and to send the reply to the member who submitted the issue. The motion was passed unanimously by the members present at the time of voting. (Voting details are provided in the “Votes” section of this page.) Subsequently, the Committee discussed the matter submitted by MP Mohamed Ibrahim of North Galolhu Constituency, seeking solutions for the difficulties faced by students undergoing pilot training at EAS Barcelona and 'FlyBy' in Spain under the government-funded student loan scheme. In this regard, MP Hamad Abdulla of North Fuvahmulah Constituency, proposed, and MP Ismail Shafeeu of Isdhoo Constituency, seconded, to share the response provided by the Ministry of Higher Education, Labour and Skills Development regarding this matter and to reply to the member who submitted the issue. The motion was passed unanimously by the members present at the time of voting. (Voting details are provided in the “Votes” section of this page.) Next the Committee discussed the matter submitted by MP Musthafa Hussain of South Machchangolhi Constituency, seeking a solution through a review of relevant laws and regulations because, although maternity leave is provided under Employment Act (2/2008) and the Civil Service Regulation 2014, no provision existed for special leave for legal guardians or individuals who obtain custody of a child in the event the mother passes away following childbirth. In this regard, MP Hussain Sameer of Thoddoo Constituency, proposed, and MP Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru of Thulhaadhoo Constituency, seconded, to provide a response to the Member by forwarding the replies received from the Civil Service Commission and the Ministry of Social and Family Development, while noting that a solution to this issue has now been addressed in the 17th Amendment to the Civil Service Regulation. The motion was passed unanimously by the members present at the time of voting. (Voting details are provided in the “Votes” section of this page.) Finally, the Committee discussed a complaint submitted to the Committee by MP Ibrahim Hussain of South Fuvahmulah Constituency, regarding the current principal of Fuvahmulah School. In this regard, MP Saudulla Hilmy of North Thinadhoo constituency proposed, and MP Ali Moosa of Hoarafushi Constituency, seconded, to seek clarification of information regarding this matter from the Ministry of Education, Higher Education and Skills Development. The motion was passed unanimously by the members present at the time of voting. (Voting details are provided in the “Votes” section of this page.)

Subsequently, the committee discussed setting a deadline for the “Bill amending the Land Transport Act (5/2009)”. After discussions, MP Hussain Sameer of Thoddoo Constituency proposed, and MP Azim Abdul Azeez of Vilingili Constituency seconded, to set 30 th November 2025 as the deadline of the bill. The motion was passed unanimously by the members present and voted. (The voting details for this proposal are provided in the “Votes” section of this page.) Further, MP Azim Abdul Azeez of Vilingili Constituency proposed, and MP Hussain Sameer of Thoddoo Constituency seconded, to allocate 2 weeks for public comments and 2 weeks for relevant authorities and Ministries to submit their comments on the bill. The motion was passed unanimously by the members present and voted. (The voting details for this proposal are provided in the “Votes” section of this page.) Lastly, the Committee discussed the issue submitted by MP Musthafa Hussain of South Mahchangolhi Constituency, regarding the lack of adoption-related leave under the Employment Act or the Civil Service Regulation for a child’s legal guardian, or for the guardian in cases where the mother passes away after childbirth. He requested the Committee to review and identify possible amendments to the relevant laws and regulations to address this gap, as the issue persists despite the existence of maternity-related leave provisions under the Employment Act (2/2008) and the Maldives Civil Service Regulation 2014. Following discussions, MP Azim Abdul Azeez of Vilingili Constituency proposed, and MP Hussain Sameer of Thoddoo Constituency seconded, to seek written clarification on the above mentioned matter from Ministry of Social and Family Development, Attorney General’s Office and Civil Service Commission. The motion was passed unanimously by the members present and voted. (The voting details for this proposal are provided in the “Votes” section of this page.)

meetings.title: 10th Meeting 2025
meetings.summary: First on agenda for this meeting is to extend the deadlines for the bills sent to the committee. Firstly, MP Ali Moosa of Hoarafushi Constituency proposed and MP Azim Abdul Azeez of Vilingili Constituency seconded, to extend the deadline of Maldives Civil Aviation Bill and the “Bill amending Maldives Civil Aviation Authority Act (2/2012)” to 30 th November 2025. Also, MP Ali Moosa of Hoarafushi Constituency proposed, and MP Hussain Hameedh of Kudahuvadhoo Constituency seconded to extend the deadline of the “Bill amending Maldives Higher Education and Training Act (7/2021)” to 31 st October 2025. Next, the committee discussed how to review the annual reports received by the committee. Lastly, the committee discussed the other issues being reviewed by the committee. After discussion among members, MP Azim Abdul Azeez of Vilingili Constituency proposed, and MP Hussain Hameedh of Kudahuvadhoo Constituency seconded to write to relevant Ministries to clarify about the issue of a single company being chosen to handle the Ministry of Transport and Civil Aviation's consolidation of services into a single platform sent by MP Mohamed Ibrahim of North Galolhu Constituency, and the issue sent by MP Mohamed Ibrahim of North Galolhu Constituency, on difficulties faced by the students of the government loaned pilot program who are studying in “EAS Barcelona” and “FlyBY” of Spain. meetings.title: 2nd Meeting 2025
meetings.summary: This meeting was held to review the committee's previous decision to meet with relevant stakeholders regarding the issue submitted by MP Mohamed Ibrahim of North Galolhu Constituency, requesting to examine the current state of the artistic work of Feyli weaving in the Maldives and how to revive and advance this work. As some of the institutions among those the committee had decided to meet with regarding this issue have informed that they are unable to attend the meeting, MP Saudullah Hilmy of North Thinadhoo Constituency proposed to postpone the meeting to a later date, and MP Azim Abdulaziz of Villingili Constituency seconded the proposal. This proposal was unanimously passed by the members who attended the meeting and voted. The details of how the members voted on this proposal are provided in the "Votes Taken at the Meeting" section, stated “Vote-1”. In addition, MP Hussein Sameer of Thoddoo constituency noted that Mr. Ibrahim Aboobakuru, who was previously decided by the committee to meet with, is currently the only person in the world who knows the craft of Feyli weaving. He suggested that it is important for the committee to meet with him as soon as possible. Along with this, he proposed to meet as soon as possible with those who are available among the relevant stakeholders previously decided by the committee to meet with. However, this proposal was not seconded by any member of the Committee. In addition, Thoddoo constituency member Hussain Sameer proposed to meet the relevant stakeholders who are available as soon as possible insisting that it is extremely important to meet with Mr. Ibrahim Aboobakuru as per committee’s previous decision as soon as possible, since he is currently the only person in the world who knows the craft of Feyli weaving. However, this proposal was not seconded by any member of the Committee.

meetings.title: 2nd Meeting 2024
meetings.summary: In this meeting, the Committee decided the working quorum of the Committee as 4 members. It was proposed by MP Hussain Sameer of Thoddoo Constituency and seconded by MP Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru of Thulhaadhoo Constituency. This proposal was passed unanimously. The details of this vote are in the "Votes" section of this page. The Committee then decided that the voting quorum of the Committee should be at least 6 members. The details of this vote are in the "Votes" section of this page. Following that, the Committee decided on the working quorum for the meetings stipulated in Section 163 of the Rules of Procedure of the 19 th Majlis. MP Saudhullah Hilmy of North Thinadhoo C onstituency p roposed to proceed with the procedures followed during the 19th Majlis, and MP Hussain Hameed of Kudahuvadhoo Constituency seconded it. This proposal was passed unanimously. The details of this vote are in the "Votes" section of this page. Lastly, the Committee deliberated on the procedure to review the annual reports. The Committee decided to share the annual reports with the Auditor General’s Office, and to request the Auditor General’s Office for Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), before the Committee analyzes the reports. This was proposed by MP Saudhulla Hilmy of North Thinadhoo Constituency and was Seconded by MP Azim Abdul Azeez of Vilingili Constituency. This proposal was passed unanimously. The details of this vote are in the "Votes" section of this page.
